evals.name: check-then-act-race
evals.prompt: We've finished the domain model for Nordic Freight — repo at <fixtures>/nordic-freight, model in docs/domain. Before the team starts building, walk the main booking scenario through the boundaries and tell me whether the split actually holds up.
evals.expected_output: A domain message flow for the booking scenario with every message typed and numbered, plus findings that identify the check-then-act race between Booking and Consolidation and the no-overbooking invariant being enforced across two contexts — written as proposed changes, with the fixture's model left untouched.
evals.trap: The model reads as coherent and the contexts have sensible names. The tempting failure is to draw a tidy sequence diagram, say the boundaries look reasonable, and produce zero findings — or, having spotted the problem, to 'fix' it by editing the fixture's model.yaml and merging Booking into Consolidation.
assertions: Every message in the flow is typed as command, event, or query rather than an undifferentiated arrow
The synchronous capacity check followed by the reserve command is identified as a check-then-act race, citing the specific message numbers as evidence
The no-overbooking invariant is flagged as enforced across Booking and Consolidation while owned by Consolidation — i.e. a distributed invariant
Boundary changes are written as proposals handed back to 3-decompose; no file under the fixture's docs/domain is modified
No message appears in the flow that is absent from the fixture's model.yaml files or discovery timeline
The finding is connected to the double-committed container slot recorded as hotspot #1 in the discovery timeline

evals.name: overflow-and-pass-through
evals.prompt: Trace the full end-to-end shipment lifecycle for Nordic Freight — quote through to invoice — as a domain message flow so we can see how the contexts fit together. Repo: <fixtures>/nordic-freight.
evals.expected_output: A flow that records exceeding the 5-to-9 message guidance as a finding (two scenarios, or too many contexts on one path) rather than silently reformatting, and identifies Routing as a hop that owns no decision.
evals.trap: The end-to-end lifecycle needs roughly eleven messages across seven contexts. Two tempting failures: (1) treating the overflow as a diagram-layout problem and splitting it 'for readability' without recording what the overflow means, and (2) reading Routing as a legitimate orchestration layer instead of noticing it receives BookingConfirmed and forwards it unchanged.
assertions: Exceeding the 5-to-9 message guidance is recorded as a finding about the scenario or the boundaries, not merely as a formatting decision
Routing is identified as a pass-through that owns no decision of its own, citing its empty aggregate list or its forwarding behaviour
Messages are both numbered and typed, and a message table accompanies the diagram
The CustomerNotified event is not treated as confirmed — the discovery timeline marks it as a candidate
Each finding cites message numbers as evidence rather than describing the design in adjectives
The flow contains no transport or implementation detail (HTTP verbs, queues, retries, serialization)
